newsitem.title: DUBAI: First Qatargas condensate cargo to sail to China.
newsitem.headline: First Qatargas condensate cargo to sail to China.

text.p: A ship to export the first cargo of condensate from the Qatargas liquefied natural gas (LNG) project has berthed at the Qatari port of Ras Laffan, oil industry sources said on Tuesday.
France's Total SA will export the condensate to China on the 15,000 tonne vessel in the next two to three days.
Condensate production from the Qatargas project is forecast to reach 30,000 barrels per day (bpd) by the end of the year, increasing to nearly 50,000 bpd by late 1998.
Qatar's current condensate exports run at some 35,000 bpd.
LNG exports from the multi-billion Qatargas project to Japan are scheduled to start in December, the first LNG shipments from OPEC member Qatar.

Qatar Liquefied Gas Co, or Qatargas, is 65 percent owned by the state Qatar General Petroleum Corp, 10 percent each by U.S. Mobil Corp and Total, and 7.5 percent each by Japan's Mitsui and Marubeni Corp.
The project is one of three LNG developments in the Gulf Arab state which will exploit the reserves of the North Field, the largest single offshore gas field in the world.
